IDN.hook: Over 17,000 islands spread across 5,000km — wider than the United States — and it is moving its capital off Java because Jakarta is sinking.
IDN.place: The great archipelago strung along the equator between mainland Asia and Australia.
IDN.borders: The Dutch East Indies inherited whole in 1949 — which is why three islands are split along colonial lines: New Guinea on the ruler-straight 141°E meridian, Borneo along the Anglo-Dutch watershed, Timor by treaty with Portugal.

PHL.hook: 7,641 islands on the Ring of Fire, and about 20 typhoons a year — more than anywhere else on Earth.
PHL.place: The archipelago north of Indonesia and east of Vietnam, facing the open Pacific.
PHL.borders: The islands Spain ruled and then sold to the US in 1898 — the Treaty of Paris literally drew a box around the archipelago, so the national territory descends from a rectangle on a colonial map.

THA.hook: The only country in Southeast Asia never colonised by a European power — it played the British and French off against each other.
THA.place: The middle of the mainland, between Myanmar and Laos, tailing south down the peninsula toward Malaysia.
THA.borders: Never colonized, so its edges are where British Burma and Malaya and French Indochina stopped: the Mekong line with Laos and the Cambodian line come from Franco-Siamese treaties of 1893–1907, the Malaysian line from a 1909 Anglo-Siamese treaty.

VNM.hook: About 1,650km long but as little as 50km wide at its waist — you can drive coast to border in under an hour in the middle.
VNM.place: The eastern edge of the mainland, an S-curve down the coast from China to the Mekong delta.
VNM.borders: The Chinese border follows the old imperial frontier as confirmed by Franco-Chinese treaties in the 1880s; the long western edge rides the Annamite mountain crest against Laos, with the Mekong delta line drawn by France inside Indochina.

MMR.hook: Produces the large majority of the world's rubies, from the Mogok valley — and answers to Burma just as often.
MMR.place: The western end of mainland Southeast Asia, between India and Thailand.
MMR.borders: British India's eastern limits: mountain arcs against India and Thailand, a Chinese line pieced together from agreements between 1894 and 1960, and the short Naf river line with Bangladesh — colonial lines drawn across highland peoples' lands.

MYS.hook: Split clean in two by the South China Sea — half a peninsula, half a slice of Borneo, 640km apart.
MYS.place: Below Thailand on the mainland peninsula, and along the north coast of Borneo beside Indonesia and Brunei.
MYS.borders: Two pieces of British empire that never touched: Malaya's line with Thailand from the 1909 Anglo-Siamese treaty, and northern Borneo's boundary along the island's central watershed against the Dutch, now Indonesian, south.

KHM.hook: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument on Earth, and Cambodia's is the only national flag anywhere that shows a building.
KHM.place: Between Thailand and Vietnam, opening onto the Gulf of Thailand.
KHM.borders: French Indochina's internal lines made international: the Thai border from 1904–07 Franco-Siamese treaties — fought over at the Preah Vihear temple as recently as 2011 — and a delta line with Vietnam that left many Khmer speakers outside.

LAO.hook: The only landlocked country in Southeast Asia, and the most heavily bombed country per person in history — unexploded ordnance is still being cleared.
LAO.place: Landlocked between Thailand and Vietnam, the Mekong running down much of its western edge.
LAO.borders: Assembled by France as a buffer along the Mekong — the river is the Thai border for most of its length, cutting the Lao-speaking world in half; the Annamite cordillera divides it from Vietnam.

TLS.hook: One of the youngest countries on Earth, independent only in 2002 after 24 years of occupation.
TLS.place: The eastern half of Timor at the far end of the Indonesian arc, just north of Australia.
TLS.borders: The Portuguese half of Timor, divided from the Dutch half by treaties finalized in 1914 — including the Oecusse enclave, Portugal's original landing point, marooned inside Indonesian West Timor.

SGP.hook: One of the last true city-states, and about a quarter larger than at independence — the extra land was reclaimed from the sea.
SGP.place: At the tip of the Malay peninsula, on the Strait of Malacca, one of the busiest shipping lanes on Earth.
SGP.borders: A trading island the British acquired in 1819; the border is the Johor Strait because Singapore was expelled from Malaysia in 1965 after two turbulent years in the federation — independence by eviction.

BRN.hook: Oil wealth means no income tax at all — and the country is split into two separate pieces by Malaysian territory.
BRN.place: Two enclaves on the north coast of Borneo, both entirely surrounded by Malaysia.
BRN.borders: The rump of a sultanate that once claimed Borneo's whole north coast, whittled away by cessions to Sarawak's Brooke rajas until Britain froze what remained in the 1880s — two separate pieces, split when Limbang was ceded in 1890.
